8390115: AArch64: Use reversed SVE shifts for variable vector operations

The change adds assembler support for the SVE LSLR and LSRR instructions
and use them for variable logical vector shifts when the shift-count
operand is single-use.

The reversed forms write the result to the shift-count register instead
of the source register. This avoids an additional copy when the source
must be preserved. For example, a variable vector rotate is expanded
into two shifts followed by an OR. The source must remain available for
both shifts. With the regular destructive LSL and LSR forms, code
generation may need to copy the source before the first shift. LSLR
and LSRR instead allow the temporary shift-count vectors to hold the
shift results, avoiding this copy.

The changes retains the existing LSL and LSR rules when the shift-count
operand has multiple uses.

According to the Arm Neoverse V1, V2, and V3 cores optimization guides
[1][2][3], LSLR and LSRR have the same performance characteristics as
LSL and LSR, respectively.

Microbenchmark testing covers ROL, ROR, LSHL, and LSHR operations for
Byte/Short/Int/LongMaxVector using the panama-vector project [4] and
test/micro/org/openjdk/bench/jdk/incubator/vector/RotateBenchmark.java.

The results show clear performance improvements on Neoverse V1, with no
significant regressions on the other tested platforms. On 128-bit SVE
platforms, such as Neoverse V2, C2 uses non-destructive NEON
instructions for left shifts with a variable shift amount, avoiding
additional moves. In contrast, right shifts use destructive SVE
instructions, where MOVPRFX fusion can help mitigate the cost of the
additional move. Using LSRR instead of LSR particularly benefits
Neoverse V1 by avoiding the additional move. See "4.18 MOVPRFX fusion"
[1] for details.

Platform: Neoverse V1
size: 1024
Mode: thrpt
Cnt: 5
Units: ops/ms
Positive values indicate improvement

Note: The regression observed in the Int/LongMaxVector.ROR cases is
caused by the change in code layout. Inserting an extra NOP before
lslr to preserve the original code layout eliminates the regression.

The table below shows the performance changes for several
code-layout variants:

* lslr+lsrr: current implementation of the patch.
* nop+lslr+nop+lsrr: insert a NOP before both sve_lslr and sve_lsrr.
* nop+lslr+lsrr: insert a NOP only before sve_lslr.
* lslr+nop+lsrr: insert a NOP only before sve_lsrr.
